etymologies.etymologyHTML: From spoke (“past participle of speak”) +‎ -s- +‎ person.

definitions.definition: A person who acts as the voice of another person or a group of people.

quote.citation: 2012, C. Holtz-Bacha, J. Strömbäck, Opinion Polls and the Media:
quote.text: News subsidies thus include making spokespersons available, producing press releases or staging pseudo-events designed to suit the media's production needs and attract the media's attention  […]

quote.citation: 2022 January 25, Eric Reinhardt, “How Joe Biden Launched a New Prison Boom”, in Slate‎[1]:
quote.text: Biden and his spokespeople have proudly touted his signature COVID relief bill as a major stimulus for policing in a national context already characterized by globally unparalleled police spending.

quote.citation: 2023 August 7, Nadeem Badshah, “Bodies of three hillwalkers recovered from ridge in Scottish Highlands”, in The Guardian‎[2], →ISSN:
quote.text: A Police Scotland spokesperson said: “We were made aware of concern for a group of three hillwalkers who had not returned from the Aonach Eagach ridge in Glen Coe shortly after 9.05pm on Saturday 5 August.
